rows.span: وقيل : إن قريشا كانوا يقولون لمن مات ذكور ولده : قد بتر فلان . فلما مات لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ابنه القاسم : بمكة ، وإبراهيم بالمدينة ، قالوا : بتر محمد ، [ ص: 198 ] فليس له من يقوم بأمره من بعده ; فنزلت هذه الآية ; قال السدي وابن زيد .

And it is said: The Quraysh used to say of the one whose male children died: "So-and-so has been cut off." When the son of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him—al-Qasim died in Mecca, and Ibrahim in Medina, they said: "Muhammad has been cut off, [for] he has no one to manage his affairs after him"; so this verse was revealed, as al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said.

qurtubi.locator: Surah108:3, displayed page 602, paragraph line 21; note internal printed page 198 at cited text.
qurtubi.wording: The full Qurtubi account states both al-Qasim in Mecca and Ibrahim in Medina, Quraysh's collective remark, and closes قال السدي وابن زيد.
qurtubi.scope: The joint attribution is exactly what Qurtubi's witness says; retain as attribution in that work, not as an authenticated chain.

suyuti.locator: Lubab al-Nuqul, reports 1233–1236; report 1233 cites Ibn Abi Hatim from al-Suddi.
suyuti.wording: Suyuti's al-Suddi inventory mentions Quraysh saying a man is cut off when male children die, then al-As ibn Wa'il saying Muhammad is cut off after the Prophet's child died.
suyuti.difference: This inventory does not give the Mecca/Medina two-son pairing, does not name Ibrahim and al-Qasim together, and does not state the joint al-Suddi/Ibn Zayd tail.

tabari.locator: Surah108:3, displayed page 602, Ibn Zayd report line 30: حدثني يونس ... أخبرنا ابن وهب ... قال ابن زيد.
tabari.wording: A distinct Ibn Zayd report says a person might call Muhammad cut off for lacking a surviving descendant.
tabari.difference: It does not give al-Suddi as co-attributor or Qurtubi's named-son/Quraysh narrative.

fidelity_finding: Arabic and English boundaries match; both place the attribution on the whole preceding account. Parallel sources provide narrower/different pieces, not the exact combined passage. Keep the shared attribution as Qurtubi's wording, do not claim independent corroboration of the complete account, and do not add a route or silently rewrite the passage.

next.task: Review the adjacent Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf report separately; distinguish Quraysh's question, Ka'b's answer, and the Qurtubi tail attribution to Ibn Abbas/Ikrimah.
